claims.claim: Zero-computation experts for dynamic per-token computation budget (18.6B-31.3B active)
claims.quote: we introduce the zero-computation experts mechanism in MoE blocks to allocate a dynamic computation budget to important tokens based on their significance
claims.ablation_quote: Validation loss curve comparing models with/without zero-computation experts under matched computation

claims.claim: Shortcut-connected MoE (ScMoE) to expand computation-communication overlap
claims.quote: we incorporate the Shortcut-connected MoE (ScMoE) [Cai et al., 2024] design to expand the computation-communication overlap window
claims.ablation_quote: Training loss curves comparing baseline models (without ScMoE) against their ScMoE-enhanced counterparts across four different model configurations

claims.claim: Hyperparameter transfer from smaller proxy models
claims.quote: We successfully apply a hyperparameter transfer strategy to such a large model, predicting optimal hyperparameter configurations by leveraging results from smaller proxy models
We initialize the model using a model-growth mechanism based on a refined half-scale checkpoint, achieving improved performance compared to conventional initialization methods
claims.ablation_quote: Validataion loss curve of a 6B activated MoE model in model growth experiments

claims.claim: Multi-pronged stability suite: router-gradient balancing, hidden z-loss, optimizer configuration
claims.quote: A multi-pronged stability suite incorporates principled router-gradient balancing, a hidden z-loss to suppress massive activations, and fine-tuned optimizer configurations
claims.ablation_quote: The introduction of a negligible-coefficient hidden z-loss stabilizes the norm curve without degrading training loss.

claims.claim: Deterministic computation for reproducibility and SDC detection
claims.quote: To enhance the reliability of large-scale cluster training, we introduce deterministic computation

claims.claim: Pre-training 560B model on 20T tokens in 30 days with 98.48% availability
claims.quote: we complete the pre-training of our 560B model over 20T tokens within 30 days and achieve 98.48% time availability

claims.claim: Inference over 100 TPS at $0.7 per million output tokens
claims.quote: large-scale deployment efficiency exceeds 100 tokens per second (TPS) on H800, with a cost of $0.7 per million output tokens

claims.claim: Two-stage pretraining data fusion strategy concentrating reasoning-intensive data
claims.quote: we design a two-stage pretraining data fusion strategy to concentrate reasoning-intensive domain data
we enhance reasoning and coding capabilities while extending the context length to 128k to meet agentic post-training requirements

claims.claim: Multi-agent synthesis framework for agentic training tasks
claims.quote: we design a multi-agent synthesis framework that defines task difficulty across three axes
we meticulously constructed two new benchmarks: Meeseeks [Wang et al., 2025a] and VitaBench

claims.claim: Competitive performance as non-thinking model with strengths in agentic tasks
claims.quote: As a non-thinking model, LongCat-Flash achieves performance comparable to state-of-the-art non-thinking models

coding.note: Ablations are loss-curve figures only, with no tables, so they are coded PARTIAL. Hidden z-loss evidence is Fig 6; Adam epsilon also has curves only (Fig 7). Router-gradient balancing and hyperparameter transfer have no shown comparison. Compute is coded N conservatively: the paper says 'tens of thousands of accelerators' and 'within 30 days', which is imprecise, so it could be argued Y. Rerun is MIXED because most comparators were evaluated in-house but some scores (marked *) come from public reports. Variance alignment (sec 2.3) was not coded because it is not stated in the abstract or intro. AIME avg@10 refers to evaluation sampling, not training seeds.
